A NEW PODCAST. THE SAME OLD COMPLAINTS. 🎉
Welcome to Another Day Ruined — a comedy help desk for life, the universe and all the minor modern dilemmas that push us over the edge.
Join Jack Dee, Seann Walsh and Sara Morgan - three friends with plenty to complain about and some questionable solutions - as they tackle the everyday irritations that can ruin your day.
This week: why can nobody understand a simple house move? When did British people start calling autumn “fall”? And why do people phone you BEFORE putting their headphones in?
Plus, wildly unreliable weather forecasts, the tyranny of the voice note, and some much-needed rules for modern phone etiquette.
But it’s not all doom and gloom. We’re also hunting for glimmers - those unexpected little moments that remind us life might not be entirely terrible.
What’s ruined your day? Tell us at hello@anotherdayruined.com, and follow @anotherdayruinedpod for clips and behind-the-scenes chaos.

results.description:
Kirsty Young's castaway this week is the comedian, Jack Dee.
Comedian, actor and writer, his persona is that of the laconic miserabilist - his hit sit-com was called "Lead Balloon" and his autobiography entitled "Thanks For Nothing". That is only part of the picture: even though show business was in the family - his great grandparents were in music hall - his early working life ranged all over the place. From grafting in the kitchens of The Ritz to working in an artificial leg factory - at one point he even seriously considered the priesthood.
He says his caustic, ironic, sarcastic comedy comes from "a sort of realism. You can't escape the dark stuff in life ... and my way of dealing with that is to absorb it into my life so that it's no longer worrying for me."

Wildlife broadcaster and conservationist Chris Packham joins Oh My Dog - and ends up answering some of the biggest dog questions we’ve ever had on the podcast.
Chris introduces us to his two poodles Sid and Nancy, explains why he feeds them a vegan diet, and reveals what science actually says about whether dogs love their owners.

It’s one of our most fascinating episodes yet!

results.description:
Kirsty Young's castaway this week is the comedian, Jack Dee.
Comedian, actor and writer, his persona is that of the laconic miserabilist - his hit sit-com was called "Lead Balloon" and his autobiography entitled "Thanks For Nothing". That is only part of the picture: even though show business was in the family - his great grandparents were in music hall - his early working life ranged all over the place. From grafting in the kitchens of The Ritz to working in an artificial leg factory - at one point he even seriously considered the priesthood.
He says his caustic, ironic, sarcastic comedy comes from "a sort of realism. You can't escape the dark stuff in life ... and my way of dealing with that is to absorb it into my life so that it's no longer worrying for me."
Producer: Cathy Drysdale.
